stem: Meera mixes lemon juice (an acid) with lime water (a base) in a glass. She adds just enough lime water so that the mixture is neither acidic nor basic. Which statement correctly explains what has happened?

options.text: The lemon juice alone became neutral after standing in the glass for some time.
Enough base was mixed with the acid so that their opposite effects cancelled, forming salt and water.
The lime water diluted the lemon juice, and dilution always makes an acid neutral.
The acid and base mixed, but any mixture of an acid and a base is always neutral.

teacher.key_rationale: Neutralisation requires a sufficient quantity of base added to the acid (or vice versa) so the resulting solution is neither acidic nor basic, producing salt and water. A omits the base; C wrongly attributes neutrality to dilution; D omits the sufficient-quantity condition. Key recalculated for the new item: B.
